olay: Qusayy ibn Kilab builds Dar al-Nadwa, the council house of Quraysh, to the north of the Ka'ba.
The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is born in Mecca in the Year of the Elephant, on the twelfth of Rabi' al-Awwal.
When the Prophet is six, his mother Amina dies at al-Abwa on the way back from Yathrib.
At about ten, the Prophet tends sheep to help his uncle Abu Talib.
At twelve, the Prophet joins a Quraysh caravan with his uncle Abu Talib and travels to Busra.
In the sacred months, the fourth Fijar war breaks out between Quraysh-Kinana and Qays 'Aylan; the Prophet is present with his uncles.
The Hilf al-Fudul pact is made in the house of 'Abdullah ibn Jud'an; the Prophet takes part.
At twenty-five, the Prophet marries Khadija.
Quraysh rebuild the Ka'ba; in the dispute over setting the Black Stone in place, the Messenger of Allah becomes the arbiter.
In the years after the Ka'ba is rebuilt, the Prophet withdraws to Hira every Ramadan to worship alone.
